explanation: Aristarchus of Samos had proposed a Sun-centred universe in the 3rd century BC, about 1,800 years earlier, but few astronomers followed him.

claims.text: Nicolaus Copernicus's book On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres, published in 1543, argued that Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun.
Galileo Galilei (born 1564), Johannes Kepler (born 1571) and Tycho Brahe (born 1546) were all born after 1543, so none of them wrote that book.
Aristarchus of Samos proposed a Sun-centred model of the universe in the 3rd century BC.
The 3rd century BC is about 1,800 years before 1543.
Aristarchus's Sun-centred idea won few followers among ancient astronomers.
